title: Laredo in Line for $35 Million to Replace Water Mains More Than 50 Years Old
excerpt: State water officials have recommended a $35 million grant for Laredo to replace about 32,000 feet of cast-iron and concrete water mains installed more than 50 years ago, with the Texas Water Development Board set to vote Dec. 3.
content:
Laredo is in line for a $35 million state grant to replace about 32,067 feet of cast-iron and concrete water mains installed more than 50 years ago, under a recommendation from the staff of the Texas Water Development Board.

The recommendation is part of $579,911,984 in one-time grants proposed for 18 of the state’s largest water systems. The three-member board is scheduled to vote on the recommendation at its 9:30 a.m. meeting Dec. 3 in Austin.

The money comes from the Water Supply and Infrastructure Grants program, created with $1.038 billion the Texas Legislature set aside in House Bill 500 in 2025. When applications closed July 30, the agency had received 695 applications seeking more than $7 billion — roughly $7 in requests for every $1 available.

Laredo is one of seven large systems recommended for the $35 million cap, alongside Corpus Christi, Arlington, Denton, Garland, the Upper Trinity Regional Water District and the North Harris County Regional Water Authority. Four of the state’s largest systems would receive the $55 million maximum.

The city has already begun replacing aging lines on its own. In June 2025, Laredo started the first phase of a citywide water line replacement project covering about 30,110 feet of old lines that had accounted for 273 water main breaks over five years and the loss of an estimated 17.2 million gallons of water.

If the board approves the recommendation, every grant must close by May 1, 2027, and all of the money must be spent by Aug. 31, 2031. Another $368,576,986 would remain for medium, small and extra-small systems, to be awarded at a later meeting.

Sources: The Texas Dispatch, Nov. 27, 2026; Texas Water Development Board staff memo for the Dec. 3, 2026 meeting; City of Laredo, June 12, 2025.
